rationale.usefulness: The protocol, inference format, catalog, renderer and application-permission boundaries are clearly separated. The migration fixture and teacher-resource, app/website review and transcript-review pilots give educational and creative builders concrete acceptance criteria. They are explicitly proposed workflows, not claimed deployments or tested SDK examples. Missing installation and cost verification limit immediate turnkey usefulness.
rationale.impact: A stable common interface contract, bidirectional calls, accessibility metadata and documented adoption across several platforms constitute a substantial development within agent-generated interfaces. The announcement and SDK tables also establish uneven protocol-version deployment. Evidence supports domain-level significance, not demonstrated field-wide transformation or independently reproduced performance gains.
rationale.novelty: Swappable generation notation targeting a common wire protocol, compact Express compilation and server-side macro expansion form a meaningful differentiated architecture. The update consolidates and stabilizes capabilities with migration changes; it does not establish an entirely new interaction paradigm. Decision-model SDK support remains future work, appropriately separated from the Apparite experiment.
rationale.maturity: The November 11 stable release, detailed migration guide and SDK compatibility tables support a usable developer pilot. Current docs explicitly describe incremental compilation and validation. However, Jetpack Compose and Gemini Enterprise remain at 0.9.1, Lynx at 0.9, macros are Python-only, package-registry versions were not checked and no live implementation or accessibility behavior was tested. Stability of the protocol is not blanket runtime dependability.
rationale.openness: Saved repository captures show Apache-2.0 licensing for A2UI and Apparite; public schemas, migration rules, SDK source links and multiple renderer/language routes provide strong inspectability and portability. Reproduction still depends on version pinning and model access; the cited measurements use hosted models and do not supply open model weights, training data or an independently reproduced runtime result. The report preserves these limits.
